newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Costello says govt to replace state taxes.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Costello says govt to replace state taxes.

text.p: Australian Treasurer Peter Costello said on Wednesday the government would replace state taxes rendered invalid by a High Court decision with federal taxes.
He said the new tax arrangements would not increase prices.
"They (the states) have indicated that these (taxes) should be considered as state taxes despite the Commonwealth being the collector," Costello told a news conference.
"The Commonwealth has agreed to that request," he said.
"No additional revenue should be collected and no price rises should take place," Costello said.
Costello said the new taxes would simply replace those revenues previously collected by the states and that all the revenues would be handed back to the states.

The High Court ruled on Tuesday that A$5 billion in state franchise fees levied on tobacco, alcohol and petrol were in fact excise taxes, which are reserved for the federal government, and thus were constitutionally invalid.

Costello said the new arrangements would be put in place legally from midnight Wednesday but they would for all purposes be seamless. "The legality is that they will be put in place from midnight," Costello said.
"The intention is to ensure it is a seamless exercise."
Costello also said the government supported reform of the indirect tax base and it was now time for state Labor parties to force to federal Labor Party to drop its opposition to indirect tax reform.
